---
title: 3 - Map view
---

Next, you will set the map's initial centre and zoom, make the map fill the browser window, and move the page styling into `style.css`.


## 3.1. Set the initial map view

- [ ] Open `main.js` and find the map configuration beginning with `const map = new Map({`.
- [ ] Inside it, locate the `view` property.
- [ ] Set the centre and zoom as shown below.

```javascript
const map = new Map({
  layers: layers,
  target: 'map',
  view: new View({
    center: [3862074, -732904],
    zoom: 6,
  }),
});
```
The `center` coordinates represent a point approximately at the center of Tanzania, and the slightly increased `zoom` parameter brings the default map view a bit closer than previously.

- [ ] Save `main.js` and refresh the webmap.

Tanzania should now be visible when the page opens, and the WMS layer with a diagonal line pattern drawn on the map.


**[SCREENSHOT 3.1: Show the map centred on Tanzania after changing the `center` and `zoom` values.]**


## 3.2. Adjust the map window

The map's centre and zoom control *what area* is shown. CSS controls *how much space* the map occupies on the page.

- [ ] Open `style.css`.
- [ ] Add the following rule at the end of the file:

```css
#map {
  position: absolute;
  top: 0;
  left: 0;
  bottom: 0;
  right: 0;
}
```

Save the file and refresh the map. It should fill the available browser window.

![*Full-screen default view of the map is now centered over Tanzania*](/images/3-1_map-view-tanzania.png)


## 3.3. Keep the HTML and CSS organised

The map's appearance has already been defined in `index.html` inside the `<style>` element. This works, but as the webmap becomes more complex, it is easier to manage all appearances in `style.css` to prevent the HTML-file expanding too much. Let's fix this.

- [ ] Open `index.html`, and examine the `<style>` section. The map window **width and height are now useless** as we already defined the window appearance in `style.css`.

`index.html`
```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <title>Single Image WMS</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="node_modules/ol/ol.css">
    <style>
      .map {
        width: 100%;
        height: 400px;
      }
    </style>
  </head>
  <body>
    <div id="map" class="map"></div>

    <script type="module" src="main.js"></script>
  </body>
</html>
```

- [ ] Remove the whole existing `<style>` section. 
- [ ] Replace the `"stylesheet"` link from `"node_modules/ol/ol.css"` to `"style.css"`.
- [ ] Set the `<title>` to a more descriptive name, such as *Tanzania forest reserves and conservation areas*. This text appears in the browser tab. It is different from a title that we will later place visibly on the map.

`index.html`
```html
!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <title>Tanzania forest reserves and conservation areas</title>

    <!-- This is custom stylesheet that refers to our style.css file -->
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
  </head>
```

- [ ] Save `index.html` and refresh the webmap.

The browser will now load the map's styling from your `style.css` file. This keeps the HTML responsible for the page structure and the CSS responsible for its appearance.


::: {.callout-note}
## Checkpoint

Your webmap should now:

- Open with Tanzania in view.
- Fill the available browser window.
- Load its custom styles from `style.css`.
- Display the correct project title in the browser tab.
:::
